children: Shares of Rays of Belief made a flat debut on the stock exchanges on Tuesday, September 8, with the stock listing at ₹239 on both the NSE and BSE, in line with its IPO issue price.

Ahead of its market debut, Rays of Belief shares were commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of ₹15, indicating a potential listing premium of around 6%. However, the stock eventually made a flat debut.

The IPO, which was open for subscription from September 1 to September 3, received an overwhelming response from investors. The issue was subscribed 107.71 times overall, with the retail portion subscribed 195.87 times, the Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) category 279.11 times and the Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) portion 9.06 times.
The ₹125-crore IPO was priced at ₹239 per share and comprised entirely a fresh issue of 52.30 lakh shares. Ahead of the public issue, the company raised ₹50 crore from anchor investors on August 31.
Rays of Belief IPO: How will the company use the funds?
The company plans to use the net proceeds primarily to expand and strengthen its learning and education infrastructure.

This includes ₹26.88 crore for setting up company learning centres and centres in partnership with licensed professionals, ₹5.54 crore for school collaboration centres, ₹2.45 crore for a Centre for Excellence and Research, and ₹2.05 crore for an Upskilling Academy.
The company has also earmarked ₹4.44 crore for technology hardware and ₹14.45 crore towards lease payments for its existing centres in India.
Another ₹10.13 crore will be invested in its US subsidiary, Moms Belief US Inc., towards lease and licence payments for existing centres in the US.

The company plans to spend ₹10.21 crore on brand awareness and inclusive outreach programmes, while a portion of the proceeds will be used to fund inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and for general corporate purposes.
The total estimated utilisation of the issue proceeds is ₹76.15 crore.

Founded in 2017, Rays of Belief is a social enterprise that offers personalised care and intervention programmes for children with neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism, ADHD, Down syndrome and cerebral palsy.

Under its Mom's Belief brand, the company has expanded its network from 71 centres in FY23 to 136 centres across 57 cities and 20 states and Union Territories as of March 31, 2026. It has a significant presence in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Its services include early intervention, occupational and language therapy, parental guidance and family support. The company had more than 340 full-time clinical professionals as of March 31, 2026.
Rays of Belief reported 125% YoY growth in total income, which rose from ₹36.54 crore in FY25 to ₹82.06 crore in FY26.
However, profitability remained under pressure despite the sharp increase in revenue. Profit after tax declined 16%, from ₹5.88 crore in FY25 to ₹4.96 crore in FY26.

title: Rays of Belief IPO: Shares list flat despite strong 108x subscription
